Blast in northern Israel near border with Lebanon wounds at least 20

Israeli medics report that at least 20 people have been injured in a blast in northern Israel near the border with Lebanon.

Israel's national emergency service, Magen David Adom said that two people are listed in serious condition, while another three are said to be moderately hurt.

The cause of the blast is thought to be the result of unexploded ordnace, but it is still being investigated by the authorities, according to Times of Israel.

Netanyahu seeks criminal charges for NAZA participants
articles.summary:
Netanyahu seeks criminal charges for NAZA participants

Submitted by Nadav Rapaport on Mon, 10/12/2026 - 13:06
Israeli prime minister escalates campaign against documentary, urging probes into insiders for alleged security breaches
An Israeli soldier behind a mounted machine gun near the Jordanian Field Hospital in Gaza City, 3 October 2025 (Jack Guez/AFP)
Off

Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has asked top officials to open an investigation into the participants of the documentary film NAZA, his office announced on Sunday.

According to the statement, the Israeli premier asked the army chief Eyal Zamir, the Shin Bet chief, David Zini, and the attorney general Gali Baharav-Miara "to act urgently to uncover the identity of all those who are involved or appear” in what he called “the libel film”.

In his letter to the three officials, Netanyahu urged them to open a criminal investigation and pursue prosecution on grounds of “serious information security offenses, criminal defamation, and harm to Israel’s diplomatic and security interests”.

The letter claims the film spreads “false, misleading and programmatic libel” against Israel and its army, causing “severe harm to Israel’s global standing”.

Netanyahu also warned that those involved may have “committed serious criminal offenses of exposing top-secret information and created a breach in the information security of a highly sensitive intelligence unit”, referring to the elite army unit 8200.

NAZA, directed by Oscar-winning Israeli filmmakers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, examines the AI-powered systems behind Israel’s mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza.

The documentary features interviews with 24 Israeli military and intelligence insiders, whose identities remain anonymous.

Muhammad Shehada, a Palestinian political analyst, argued on X that "Netanyahu accidentally confirms NAZA's exposé", noting that while officials previously dismissed the film as a “hoax”, the Israeli premier is now saying NAZA revealed classified information.

As Netanyahu seeks a sixth term ahead of the 27 October elections and polls show him trailing former army chief Gadi Eisenkot, the Israeli PM has made NAZA a prominent target in his re-election campaign, repeatedly attacking the documentary.

On Sunday, Israeli media reported that leaked WhatsApp messages from his closest adviser Yonatan Urich suggested that right-wing Channel 12 journalist Amit Segal advised his campaign to leverage the NAZA controversy.

Wider attacks

Since the film won the Special Jury Prize at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival last month, Israeli politicians, journalists, social media users and far-right protesters have attacked the film's creators, accusing them of treason.

As elections loom, NAZA controversy strikes at the heart of Israel's crisis
Read More »

Last month, Israeli army chief Zamir instructed military officials to seek legal actions against the filmmakers and the soldiers who testified in it.

Meanwhile, the Israeli military released a 17-page response to the film, stating it "falsely portrays a military that seeks to cause civilian harm".

Netanyahu and Culture Minister Miki Zohar also asked for the revocation of the Israeli citizenships of Abraham and Szor, with Zohar urging Shin Bet chief Zini last week to investigate Abraham's alleged connections to Hamas.

Szor told The Guardian podcast Stateside that the violent Israeli backlash against the film is "scary".

Last month, far-right demonstrators gathered outside her parents’s home in central Israel, calling for her and Abraham to be hanged for treason.

"We made this film so people would talk about it, and we also received support from a small part of Israeli society that opposes Israel's policies over the years," Szor said.

articles.title: Gaza: ‘She survived the bombing, but not the blockade’
articles.summary:
Gaza: ‘She survived the bombing, but not the blockade’

After two years of bombardment and forced displacement during Israel’s genocide in Gaza, Suhaila al-Mabhouh had one wish: to go home.

The 60-year-old Palestinian longed so desperately to return to her family home in northern Gaza that she turned down an evacuation offer to Italy, submitted by her daughter, who lives there.

When the so-called ceasefire took effect on 10 October 2025, she and her husband rushed back to their home in Jabalia refugee camp.

She began making small repairs to the badly damaged house, hoping to piece her life back together after two years of bombardment.

But the hope of rebuilding was short-lived, as Israel maintained its siege and continued its daily bombardment.

Read more: Gaza: ‘She survived the bombing, but not the blockade’

articles.title: Palestinian succumbs to wounds sustained in Israeli attack in northern Gaza
articles.summary:
Palestinian succumbs to wounds sustained in Israeli attack in northern Gaza

A Palestinian man has died from wounds sustained in an Israeli attack in northern Gaza, Wafa news agency reports, citing medical sources.

According to the sources, Khaled Abdel-Fattah Jaber, died from wounds sustained in an Israeli drone strike on Sunday.

In a separate attack, another Palestinian was wounded by Israeli fire near Abu Hamid Roundabout, east of Khan Younis city in Gaza's south.

Al Jazeera reports that Jaber's death brings the total number of people killed in Gaza on Monday to three, with two others killed in a drone attack in Rafah.

According to Gaza's health ministry Israel has killed at least 1,493 and wounded another 5,299 since the so-called ceasefire was implemented a year ago.

archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, persistent security risks in the Persian Gulf tied to tanker attacks and ongoing IDF operations in the north and Gaza are expected.

archive.security_status_cs: Bezpečnostní situace v regionu zůstává vysoce napjatá po zprávách o explozích na severu Izraele s desítkami zraněných a incidentech v Perském zálivu a okolí Kataru, kde byly zasaženy ropné tankery. Izraelské operace v Gaze a napětí na libanonské hranici nadále zatěžují regionální stabilitu.
archive.security_status_en: The regional security situation remains highly tense following reports of explosions in northern Israel injuring dozens and maritime incidents in the Persian Gulf and near Qatar involving targeted oil tankers. Israeli operations in Gaza and friction along the Lebanese border continue to strain regional stability.

archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, heightened vigilance in Gulf maritime transport and persistent tactical clashes along the Israel-Lebanon border are expected.

archive.security_status_cs: Bezpečnostní situace v regionu zůstává vysoce napjatá v důsledku incidentů na izraelsko-libanonské hranici, kde nedávný výbuch zranil desítky lidí. Přetrvávající napětí v Perském zálivu podtrhují útoky na plavidla v okolí Kataru a přetrvávající operace íránských dezinformačních sítí. V Sýrii a Iráku navíc sílí diskuse o postavení kurdské menšiny a ústavních zárukách.
archive.security_status_en: The regional security situation remains highly tense due to incidents along the Israel-Lebanon border, where a recent blast injured dozens of people. Ongoing tensions in the Persian Gulf are underscored by attacks on vessels near Qatar and continued operations by Iranian disinformation networks. Additionally, discussions regarding the status of the Kurdish minority and constitutional guarantees are gaining traction in Syria and Iraq.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračující taktické střety na izraelsko-libanonské hranici a zvýšené bezpečnostní prověřování v oblasti Perského zálivu. Diplomatické třenie mezi Izraelem a evropskými státy pravděpodobně zůstanou na zvýšené úrovni.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, continuing tactical clashes along the Israel-Lebanon border and heightened security vetting in the Persian Gulf region are expected. Diplomatic friction between Israel and European states is likely to remain elevated.

archive.security_status_cs: Bezpečnostní situace v regionu zůstává vysoce napjatá po incidentech na izraelsko-libanonské hranici, kde výbuch zranil desítky lidí. Nervousness is also rising in the Persian Gulf region due to attacks on maritime and tanker shipping, while Iranian disinformation campaigns and political friction in Gaza and Syria further destabilize regional stability.
